_what: Handlers performing two or more writes with no explicit transaction. They are atomic only because tenantMiddleware wraps the whole request in one — a property they never asked for.
_why_this_matters: That transaction exists for ISOLATION (SET LOCAL ROLE + the tenant GUC). Atomicity is a side effect of where its boundary sits. Moving the boundary — which the concurrency ceiling requires — turns each of these into a silent partial write.
_how_to_fix: Wrap the handler body in db.transaction().execute(async (trx) => …) and use trx for every write. Then remove the file from this list.
_reasons_are_preserved: Entries under _reasons survive --update. A file listed there is one a reviewer has looked at and decided does NOT need wrapping — helpers that run inside a caller's transaction, or branches that are mutually exclusive so only one write ever executes. The count still has to match, so a NEW write in such a file still fails the gate.

_reasons.ext:billing/engine/lib/stripe-client.ts: applyStripeEvent() runs inside handleWebhook's transaction — the caller owns the boundary. Its three writes are also mutually exclusive switch branches, so only one ever executes. Covered by stripe-webhook-atomicity.test.ts.
_reasons.ext:communications/mail/engine/routes.ts: Four handlers, none of which should be wrapped. POST /oauth/callback consumes the single-use state row BEFORE the token exchange ON PURPOSE — a code that fails to exchange must not leave a state usable for a second attempt; a transaction spanning the exchange would roll the consumption back and reopen exactly the replay window that comment closed, while also holding the transaction across a network call. POST /bulk, GET /messages/:id and DELETE /messages/:id write once per invocation (mutually exclusive switch branches, or independent idempotent cache writes) and their other statements are IMAP round trips.
_reasons.ext:communications/mail/engine/lib/compo: saveDraft() is `existing ? UPDATE (and return) : INSERT` — exactly one write executes.
_reasons.ext:communications/mail/engine/lib/sieve: executeLocalActions() applies one write per action inside a per-action try/catch, deliberately so one failing filter action does not stop the rest. NOTE, separately from atomicity: that catch cannot contain a FAILED SQL statement while this runs inside a surrounding transaction — Postgres refuses everything after it — so the containment is only real once the tenant transaction stops spanning the request. Tracked as its own problem, not fixed by wrapping.
_reasons.ext:communications/mail/engine/lib/imap-: syncImapAccount() now wraps message+attachments per message. The remaining flagged writes are the folder upsert and the per-folder last_uid advance, which must commit independently: a sync that fails on message 900 of 1000 must keep the 899 it already stored.
_reasons.ext:compliance/ro/efactura/engine/routes: Two remaining, both single-write-per-invocation. saveSettings() is `prev ? UPDATE : INSERT`. POST /oauth/exchange writes `last_error` in two error branches that each return immediately, or the tokens on success — exactly one runs. POST /:id/submit deliberately keeps the daily-stats aggregate OUTSIDE its transaction: it is recomputable, and rolling the submission record back over it would make the invoice look unfiled while ANAF already has it, causing a double filing.
_reasons.ext:auth/scim/engine/routes.ts: setActive() takes the transaction handle as its first parameter — the caller (PUT, PATCH, POST) owns the boundary. Covered by deactivation-atomicity.test.ts, which fails on a version without it.
_reasons.ext:operations/pos/engine/routes.ts: claimOrderNumber(dbh) takes the handle as its parameter — every caller wraps it. Its two statements are an upsert of the counter row plus the UPDATE … RETURNING that allocates, and allocating outside the sale's transaction is exactly what the callers now avoid.
_reasons.ext:data/import/engine/routes.ts: runImport() runs entirely inside ctx.internals.withTenantIsolation(), which gives the whole job one transaction — a background task has no request transaction to inherit, so it opens its own. POST /:collection writes the job row; its second flagged write is the after-response failure recovery, which deliberately opens a SEPARATE tenant transaction because the request's is already committed by the time it runs.
_reasons.ext:content/documents/engine/routes.ts: getNextDocNumber(dbh, …) takes the handle — the caller owns the boundary — and its writes are the two arms of `seq ? UPDATE : INSERT`, so exactly one runs.
_reasons.ext:content/pages/engine/editor.ts: PUT /menus/:key is a hand-written upsert: `UPDATE … RETURNING id`, and the INSERT runs only when it matched nothing, so exactly one write executes. (It does race two concurrent first-writes into a unique violation — a concurrency question the comment there explains, not an atomicity one, and a transaction would not fix it.)
_reasons.packages/engine/src/routes/backup.ts: POST / writes the backup row in the request, then the background task updates it to completed OR failed — two mutually exclusive branches, one of which runs. That task uses poolDb (backupRoutes is mounted with poolDb, not the request proxy), so it is correctly outside any request boundary. POST /schedules/:id/trigger now wraps each outcome branch, because there the backup status and the schedule's last_run_status are the same fact recorded twice.
_reasons.packages/engine/src/routes/sync.ts: POST /push performs ONE write per operation: a bulk INSERT for the creates of a collection, then update OR delete per non-create op. Deliberately NOT wrapped: `effectiveDb` is `c.get('tenantTrx')`, a raw Kysely Transaction, and Kysely throws "calling the transaction method for a Transaction is not supported" — unlike ctx.db in extensions, which is the proxy that joins. SEPARATE KNOWN DEFECT, resolved by the boundary move rather than by wrapping: the per-op try/catch cannot contain a failed SQL statement while the whole push runs inside the request transaction, so one bad record makes every later op fail and the response reports them as independent errors. Once the boundary moves off the request each op autocommits and the per-op handling becomes correct.
_reasons.packages/engine/src/routes/insights.ts: POST /panels/:id/execute writes the result cache and the panel's execution stats. insightsRoutes is mounted with poolDb, so each statement autocommits and the deliberate `.catch` on the cache upsert genuinely IS contained — a cache miss only costs a re-run. Not the poisoning pattern that the same code would be inside a request transaction.
_reasons.packages/engine/src/routes/revisions.ts: DELETE /record/comments/:commentId deletes through one of two mutually exclusive branches (admin deletes any, everyone else only their own), so exactly one statement runs.
_reasons.packages/engine/src/routes/schema-branch: POST /branches creates the branch SCHEMA, copies collection and relation metadata into it, and writes the zv_schema_branches row LAST, with an explicit compensating `DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE` on failure. The ordering is already the safe one and the compensation is correct; wrapping would replace working code with a behaviour change for no gain.
_reasons.ext:storage/cloud/engine/routes.ts: POST /favorites/:fileId is a toggle — DELETE and return, or INSERT and return. POST /admin/quotas is `existing ? UPDATE (and return) : INSERT`. Exactly one write runs in each.
_reasons.ext:storage/cloud/engine/lib/file-versio: createFileVersion(db, …) takes the handle, and its writes are interleaved with putObject/deleteObject calls to object storage. Wrapping it would hold a database transaction across network uploads — the pattern that pins pool connections on something that is not the database's fault — and object storage cannot roll back anyway, so the transaction would buy consistency for half the operation only. The cleanup loop was reordered instead (row before object) so the cheaper failure is the one that can happen.
